plotting_plan.title: Classification pipeline with optional large-model hand-off
plotting_plan.objective: Block diagram (left to right): input fields (title, artist/channel, site, duration) -> normalisation -> site rules -> hashed character n-gram features (2^17 buckets) -> three int8 linear heads (type 4, genre 10, video class 2) with artist-table logit bonus -> thresholds -> label or abstain; a dashed branch from 'combined confidence < tau' to a server-side large language model. Annotate on-device part with '2.1 MB, <1 ms, identical in 4 runtimes'.

plotting_plan.title: Model size versus fully-right accuracy on the real test set
plotting_plan.objective: Scatter plot with log-scale x axis (model file size in MB) and y axis fully-right accuracy (%) on the 383-item real test set with 95% Wilson interval error bars, for: linear round 1, linear round 5 (shipped), linear without chart data, transformer fp32, linear+transformer; DeepSeek and the hybrid drawn as horizontal reference lines labelled 'server'. Shows that 200x more parameters bought nothing.

plotting_plan.title: Accuracy versus share of items handed to the large model
plotting_plan.objective: Line chart: x = share of items sent to DeepSeek (%), y = fully right (%), one line per evaluation set (real test, real dev, focus, synthetic) with markers at thresholds 0, 0.5, 0.6, 0.7, 0.8, 0.85, 0.9, 0.95 and 'always'; mark tau = 0.9 on the real-test line; horizontal dashed line for DeepSeek alone on real test.

plotting_plan.title: Per-genre accuracy on real test music items
plotting_plan.objective: Grouped horizontal bar chart over the ten genres (with n per genre in the label): shipped linear, linear without chart data, DeepSeek. Sorted by the gap between DeepSeek and shipped linear, so anime, lofi, hiphop and other appear together, supporting the knowledge-gap explanation.

plotting_plan.title: Synthetic validation overstates accuracy
plotting_plan.objective: Dot-and-line (dumbbell) chart for rounds 1, 2 and 5: genre accuracy when answered on the synthetic test split versus the real test set, with the gap in points labelled (15.3, 13.6, 10.5).

introduction_strategy.hook_hypothesis: Media-aware applications (players, companions, recommenders) increasingly need to know what is playing, but often only see the text metadata a browser or OS exposes, not the audio; doing this on device protects privacy and works offline.
introduction_strategy.problem_gap_hypothesis: Music genre classification is mostly studied from audio or lyrics, and text classification from metadata is studied mainly in English; there is little evidence on how far a tiny on-device model can go on short, multilingual (EN/JA/ZH) media titles, what limits it, and whether stronger on-device learners (LLM distillation, small multilingual transformers) close the gap to large language models. Scope claims to this single task and its 383-item real test set.
search_directions: Surveys of music genre classification and music information retrieval, including audio-based and text/lyrics-based approaches
Foundational work on efficient linear text classification with n-gram features and the hashing trick (feature hashing, fastText)
Work on on-device or privacy-preserving machine learning inference and model compression (quantisation)
Large language models as zero-shot or few-shot text classifiers and annotators
Surveys or studies of synthetic data generated by large language models for training and evaluating classifiers

related_work_strategy.overview: Position the work against four lines: metadata/text-based music and media classification, efficient hashed n-gram linear models, compact multilingual transformers and knowledge distillation, and cascades / selective prediction that combine a small model with a large one. Cutoff 2026-10-01.

subsections.subsection_title: 2.1 Music and media classification from text and metadata
subsections.methodology_cluster: Genre or content classification from lyrics, titles, artist names, tags or playlists
subsections.sota_investigation_mission: Find papers that classify music genre or media type from lyrics, track titles, artist names, social tags or other metadata, including multilingual or East Asian music, published before 2026-10-01. Do not look for new competitors to benchmark.
subsections.limitation_hypothesis: These approaches rely on lyrics or rich tags, or on English-only data; short titles carry little linguistic signal and genre depends on knowing the artist.
limitation_search_queries: music genre classification from lyrics deep learning
music genre classification metadata artist name text
cross-lingual lyrics genre classification Japanese Chinese
subsections.bridge_to_our_method: We work with the title, artist, site and duration alone, in three languages, and make artist knowledge an explicit updatable table rather than something the model must learn.

subsections.subsection_title: 2.2 Efficient linear text classifiers and feature hashing
subsections.methodology_cluster: Bag of n-grams, character n-grams, hashing trick, fastText-style linear models, quantised compact classifiers
subsections.sota_investigation_mission: Find foundational and recent papers on hashed n-gram features, character n-gram models for multilingual or unsegmented text, fastText and its compression, and strong linear baselines for short-text classification.
subsections.limitation_hypothesis: Linear n-gram models capture surface patterns but cannot know entity facts (which artist plays which genre) beyond what appears in training data.
limitation_search_queries: fastText compressing text classification models quantization
feature hashing large scale multitask learning
character n-gram text classification Chinese Japanese without segmentation
subsections.bridge_to_our_method: We adopt the hashed character n-gram linear model for its size, speed and portability, and add site rules and an artist lookup to supply knowledge it cannot learn.

subsections.subsection_title: 2.3 Compact multilingual transformers and knowledge distillation
subsections.methodology_cluster: Multilingual pretrained encoders (XLM-R, mBERT), small distilled encoders (MiniLM, DistilBERT), knowledge distillation and LLM-generated labels
subsections.sota_investigation_mission: Find the papers introducing XLM-R, multilingual MiniLM / MiniLMv2, DistilBERT, knowledge distillation, and studies that use large language models to label or generate training data for smaller classifiers.
subsections.limitation_hypothesis: Distillation transfers decision boundaries learnable from inputs, but cannot transfer entity knowledge into a model whose capacity or input representation cannot store it; small encoders also carry large vocabulary embeddings that dominate size.
limitation_search_queries: knowledge distillation from large language models into small text classifiers limitations
large language model annotation for text classification training data quality
subsections.bridge_to_our_method: We test both routes directly (LLM-labelled data and relabelling; a 107M-parameter mMiniLMv2) and find neither improves real-world accuracy, supporting a knowledge-gap explanation.

subsections.subsection_title: 2.4 Cascades, selective prediction and model routing
subsections.methodology_cluster: Confidence-based abstention and deferral from a small model to a large model
subsections.sota_investigation_mission: Find papers on selective classification / reject option, model cascades and LLM routing or cascading for cost reduction (e.g. sending queries to larger models only when needed), and calibration of classifier confidence.
subsections.limitation_hypothesis: Cascade work usually targets cost of large models on hard NLP tasks; on-device privacy constraints and the complementary-error effect for tiny models are less studied.
limitation_search_queries: LLM cascade cost reduction query routing small model large model
selective classification reject option deep neural networks
calibration of modern neural network confidence
subsections.bridge_to_our_method: Our hybrid defers only the ~32% of items below a confidence of 0.9 and matches or exceeds sending everything to the large model.
